steps: Write down the oven settings: 400F, 15 minutes.
Lower the temperature: 400 minus 25 is 375F, and the time stays 15 minutes.
Or shorten the time: 15 × 0.75 = 11.25, rounded to 11 minutes, at the same 400F.

felicityNote: Salmon is the fish to learn first. One inch thick, 12 minutes, opaque in the middle. Once you have that, every other fish follows.

parts.meaning: The air fryer runs hotter than the dial says, because the fan pushes hot air straight onto the food. Dropping 25F keeps the outside from drying out before the centre cooks.
When you lower the temperature, the food still needs the full oven time. The lower heat and the full time balance each other out.
A quarter sooner. Keep the oven temperature and check at three quarters of the oven time. Open the basket then, because the window between done and dry is short.
The safe internal temperature for fish. The flesh should be opaque all the way through and flake easily with a fork.

formula.text: Pick one, never both. Lower the temperature: air fryer temp = oven temp minus 25F, and the time stays the same. Or shorten the time: keep the oven temperature and check at oven time × 0.75. For fish at 400F for 15 minutes: either 375F for 15 minutes, or 400F and check at about 11 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Read the oven settings
howToSteps.text: Find the temperature and time in your recipe. Fish fillets usually bake at 400F for 12 to 15 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Pick one change
howToSteps.text: Pick one change, not both. Either take 25F off the temperature and keep the time, or keep the temperature and check a quarter sooner. 400F for 15 minutes becomes either 375F for 15 minutes or 400F and check at about 11 minutes.

howToSteps.name: Oil and place
howToSteps.text: Brush the fillets with a little oil and lay them on parchment in a single layer, skin side down.

howToSteps.name: Cook and check early
howToSteps.text: Check early. Pull the fish at 145F, or when the flesh flakes easily with a fork.

lede: Fish fillets that bake at 400F for 15 minutes air fry two ways: 375F for the full 15 minutes, or 400F and check at about 11 minutes. Pull them at 145F, when the flesh flakes easily.

title: Oven to Air Fryer: Fish Fillets
tutorial: Fish is the fastest cook in the air fryer, and the one with the smallest margin. A salmon fillet that bakes at 400F for 15 minutes air fries two ways: 375F for the full 15 minutes, or 400F and check at about 11 minutes. The difference between done and dry is about two minutes either way.

Fish is done at 145F inside, or when the flesh turns opaque all the way through and separates easily with a fork. Either test works. The thermometer is the surer one, because a fillet can look done on the outside while the centre is still translucent. Measure in the thickest part.

Oil the fish, not the basket. Brush the fillets with a little oil before they go in, because fish sticks to a dry crisper plate. A sheet of parchment under the fillets makes the clean-up trivial, and the fish holds it down so the fan cannot lift it.

Thickness decides the time more than the species does. A one-inch fillet takes the full converted time at 375F. A half-inch fillet takes about half of it. A thick steak takes longer. The converted time assumes a typical fillet, so adjust by thickness and check early the first time you cook a new fish.

Do not flip delicate fish. Salmon and cod fall apart when you turn them halfway, and the air fryer does not need it. The hot air reaches the bottom through the crisper plate, and one side down the whole cook gives you a fillet in one piece. Breaded fish is the exception: flip it once so both sides crisp.
